hens_rule_text: Up to 5 hens on a single-family lot with the coop outside all required setbacks; more are allowed farther from property lines (up to 15 hens at 15 ft from property lines, up to 25 hens if the coop is 50 ft from any residence).
permit_notes: No permit is described for keeping chickens on a single-family lot, community garden or retail farm; the limits are set purely by setback distance.
setback_notes: Municipal Code Sec. 131.0443 sets setbacks from property lines by zone, not a flat distance from neighboring homes; the 25-chicken tier requires the coop to be at least 50 ft from any residential building.
coop_rules: Coop and outdoor enclosure must be predator-proof, easily cleaned, well ventilated, fenced to keep chickens on the property, and provide at least 10 sq ft per chicken in the outdoor run.
zoning_notes: Allowed on single-family residential properties, community gardens and retail farms per Municipal Code Sec. 42.0709, added in 2012.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: City of San Diego, Chickens (Urban Farming, Bees and Livestock)
San Diego Humane Society, Keeping Chickens in the City of San Diego

research_notes: Read the live official city page directly, which states the full 'Summary of Regulations' plainly (5/15/25 chicken tiers by setback, no roosters, coop specs). Did not separately open Municipal Code Sec. 42.0709 or Sec. 131.0443 text, but the city page states it summarizes them.
